Have you ever hit rock bottom? What got you there? Where are you now?

Embarrassed the fuck out of my parents in front of their guests asking for a gun, or if one of them would be so kind as to kill me (my actual words). They gave me a bowl in case I had to vomit, but I tried to bite a chunk out of it so I could choke on it. They took me to the hospital, I continued trying to get people to kill me. A nurse put in a cathader and I tried to bite her. My brother came and picked me up later that night and let me crash on his couch. I woke up and had no idea where I was so I left and called my friend to come get me. I was down on myself for a while, but realized it wasn't helping. I'm better now though. Also, I think I had a stroke that night.
I think it would be hard to not be better now
they dont call it rock bottom for nothing lol

I'll post this on this account because no one knows it... yet...

So my rock bottom would have to be the fourth of July this year. To make a long story short, I got blackout drunk, went into the bathroom at my friend's place, took off my pants, tied them around my neck and the shower curtain bar thing, and tried to kill myself. If I would have succeeded, my friend would have found me covered in puke, with no pants or underwear on, hanging from a shower curtain. It wouldn't have been a pretty sight.

After talking me out of it, my friend got me out and laid me down on the couch. After he had told everyone there what had happened, his girlfriend got on top of me and started to make out with me. So to add to my suicide attempt, my friend's girlfriend cheats on him with me while he's still in the room.

I then puked (in a bucket thank god) and passed out.

The little fiasco has got me thinking. I had been seeing a psychiatrist to sort out my depression but never wanted to go on medication. After that night, I made the decision to take whatever steps necessary to stay sober and not end my life. If that means meds, so be it. If it means admittance into a hospital, so be it. I just don't want to end my life this early.

Sorry for the long winded response. I know there are probably much worse cases out there but right now, there's only one comment and I figured I should add whatever I could.

Speaking from second hand experience (loved ones and close friends). Everyone I know who has gone into a psych ward came out worse than they were. Unless you feel like you're literally on the edge of a bridge ready to jump, seek out anything else than being incarcerated. Everyone that I've known who's gone in has told that being in there makes you feel more crazy than you actually are.

The time I spent in jail was not nearly as bad as the day I was sentenced to felony probation. Even after the incarceration I was still an irresponsible little shit. It was only when the judge told me that If I don't walk the straight and narrow for a while not only would I go to prison, but I would have a black mark on my record that leaves me unable to do anything but the lowest paying and most menial jobs for the rest of my life. I'm getting my associates in a few weeks and am going to university this fall. rock bottom is when I get the feeling that all this work is meaningless, when that happens I just tell myself to at least see this through to the end.
Congrats man. All that work isn't meaningless, at the very least it'll keep you away from crime.

I'm a non-practicing alcoholic. Now, my rock bottom wasn't some sort of catastrophic event that led to a period of reflection then subsequent sobriety. My rock bottom came when I realized that I had no more money to get drunk. I was going through my finances one night and realized that I was tapped (on unemployment at the time). My wife was 3 days away from payday and didn't have a dime. I remember sitting there going "Hmmmm. Having to be sober for 3 days is gonna suck. It sure would be cool if I didn't have to worry about this anymore." Went to rehab 2 days later. Haven't drank since (5 years). As a sidenote: On my way to rehab, I stopped to get gas and get a scratch ticket. I won $500. Used the winnings to help pay the insurance deductible. True story.
I wanted to upvoat this, but i am at my 24 hour limit, and cant. this really hit home with me, and great job staying sober my internet stranger friend!

Yes, absolutely. It didn't involve addiction or anything like that, but it most definitely happened. I was 23, had 2 kids and the wife left. I had a decent job, but we lived out in the country and I drove pretty far...more than 40 miles each way to work. Things weren't going to work out with my wife and my brother lived much closer to my job, do I moved in with him and his wife.

I was really devastated by the split. I was on the verge of not being able to function because of it. I wound up quitting my job for another one that was no where near as good. I felt like I needed the change. I got myself a tiny apartment real close to my new job and threw myself into it.

The problem is, I never dealt with the issues, I avoided it, so nothing ever really got better. Then my vehicle got stolen, was used in a crime, wrecked and held as evidence. This caused the insurance claim to get held in limbo so I could be get a new car. I could walk to work, so there was that...until I blew out a knee.

No work, no vehicle and a bum knee. I couldn't go see my kids and It didn't take long to get evicted. I wasn't going back my brother, so instead, I called my grandmother who lived 250 miles away. I moved up there, had a job within a week and access to a vehicle. It took a few years, but I was able to build my life back and it was far better than where I was.

It was a tough time, but very necessary for who I am today. I'm very much an optimist about life and my philosophy is to nut up and figure it out instead of wallow in excuses why you can't do it. The quickest way to get past adversity it to face it and walk straight through it than to avoid it.

Went through a nasty breakup with a girl I'd poured an insane amount of my life energy into, who broke it off almost casually over Facebook message, cited "not wanting to be in a relationship," then almost immediately started dating my best friend at the time (not my best friend anymore, mind you). I wrote an EP about it, then spent a month distracting myself by making ska covers of classic pop songs, then my recording computer shat the bed and I ended up feeling rudderless. So what did I do? I had been an occasional weed user previously, but I started smoking weed all the time now. My fitness level dropped, my brain was always slow and sluggish, I stopped caring about school or doing my homework, I was basically just full-on stoner mode, spent my days getting stoned, watching random bullshit on Youtube, and noodling on my guitar. Finally, the end of the school year came around and I found out that I'd failed two of my three classes, got myself in bad academic standing, and also failed to complete enough prereqs to declare my major by the school's imposed deadline, meaning I now had a one-year enrollment hold.

So now I'm spending the year taking community college classes to get up to major declaration point. Only thing I can really do at this point is keep on keepin' on.

Yeah! I used to drink a lot. Like a lot a lot. Not like, "Haha, 20's, amirite?" I drank like probably a bottle of 100 proof peppermint schnapps every day for 3 years or so, and before that it was at least beer or wine or whatever. Every day. I wasn't sober for more than 12 hours for like 5 or 6 years.

I'd wake up, puke, get a glass of water, chug it, puke, put my phone in a bag and sit in the shower fucking around on the internet, because those were the only two places I could go to escape the panic attacks. Well, the bottom of a rumpleminze bottle was the third, but I literally couldn't stock it at my house or I'd end up going to work drunk. I drank a ton at work though. Oh, right.

I worked at family-owned bars almost exclusively through this. With my mom. Who didn't realize how bad off I was getting. I went into the ER for kidney stones, and I had to clarify to the nurses that, "I don't know, way too many," wasn't a joke when they asked me how many drinks I had every week. Usually, showing them the whites of my eyes, and how they weren't white anymore, silenced any, "oh ha ha I know how that goes" talk before it began.

I couldn't do anything besides drink. It was literally killing me, and it caused my girlfriend of 3 and a half years to leave. 2 days before the kidney stones. That was fun.

Anyway at this point my family had opened a bar a year and a half prior, and we weren't doing great. Couldn't cash my checks, we couldn't afford to make repairs, bounced checks to vendors all the time, and my mom and I were constantly screaming at each other. Most of the time also drunk. It was not ideal, and it was headed south VERY fast.

I had a bit of an awakening when the nurse said, "You're going to be in deep shit if you don't stop drinking. Your liver looks like what we see in old men who have been drinking for 30 years." I had no money, my girlfriend left me, my family's business was going to tank, and my family relationships were fucked because of the booze.

I invited my best friend and co-worker to move in with me. He's a career Army veteran and a fitness enthusiast. I decided that I had to quit drinking. There wasn't really a choice, I was too much of a pussy to die young and I hadn't had a chance to get rich yet. I tapered off of booze while I worked out every day, ate right, took all my vitamins and drank tons of water. I put on like 20 lbs and went up a shirt and pants size because of it. I stopped smoking a few months later, and eventually found the balance between body builder and normal dude. Things were good.

Other than my mom still being an addict. She was in control of the business, and with sober eyes came a clarity of the way things were working at the business. And it was awful. No matter how we did in sales, somehow we were always in the red. We would sell $40,000 in one month which for us was amazing, and I'd still get drunkenly berated for daring to cash my paychecks and overdrawing the account when the "owner" couldn't pay herself. Never mind the fact that I had no access to any of the accounts.

Fast forward a few months, now I own the bar by myself. It's been an arduous journey, and it isn't over. But I managed to clear $10,000 of tax debt in 30 days while still maintaining vendor accounts, payroll, rent and utilities, in one of the slowest months of the year. So I got that going for me, which is nice.

The way I came to own the place is not ideal. It was like a collapse of all of the walls my mother had built to keep everyone out of her painful, dark reality. She'd constructed herself a fortress of coping mechanisms and defensive behavior, mortared together and reinforced by manipulation and self loathing. The grounds seeded with deprecation and patrolled by enablers. She was deaf to the outside for all of the echoes of her own torment, bouncing off of the cold walls and reverberating into her head. I can only hope that one day soon I can help her find the strength that I found to overcome debilitating addiction and depression. Until then, I'm going to continue to fight on with this business and attempt to get her shit back, which was seized by the land lord in a lien for a huge debt.

A lot of people have had it worse than me, but nothing is impossible! If anyone has problems with addiction, depression, any shit like that, consider this my invitation to shoot me a message and talk about it. I probably should have used an alt for this, but fuck it.

be careful with your actions and words. You might not realize what damage it can do to another

800g ground chicken
One red onion
2dl Sour Cream
Black beans (as much as you want)
Jalapeños (as much as you want)
One pack of tikka masala spice mix
Stir.

When cooked you add veggies:
Cucumber
Corn
Red Pepper
and what ever floats your boat.

Turn your oven on 250c and put in your taco wraps.
Then EAT and enjoy

2 Chainz Is Being Sued For Calling Someone A "Thot" On Youtube
I think acurately discribes the situation. Unless of course they can show that they were negatively impacted financially.
Sounds like she should be suing the manager who fired her if anybody, sounds like she just wants to cash in off a rich guy who vaguely maybe sorta hurt her reputation.

With libel or slander, you don't just have to prove that someone said something malicious about you, you have to prove damages. Which is extremely hard to do. What they're counting on with a frivolous law suit like this, is that 2chainz attorneys will determine it is cheaper to settle with the crazy person than it is to have a long court battle (which it usually is).

If it goes to trial, this lady will hands down lose. The question now, is how much "fuck off" money 2chainz is willing to settle with to get this psycho to do just that. Her own lawyers will want to settle as again, if it goes to trial, they lose and are likely on a contingency fee and will make nothing at all that way. If it settles, they'll get around half of the settlement.

I would expect the (of course undisclosed) amount of settlement will probably be between 100k and 200k realistically. If she lets it go to trial thinking she'll get more, she'll get nothing and lose nothing.
Judging by the legal assessment of the situation, and the team of highly skilled lawyers. She'll get about tree fiddy

It's better than a 90 percent chance she'll get some form of settlement, as less than 10 percent of civil cases make it to an actual trial before settlement occurs. Reading the article, she might be capable of proving some damages, as her place of employment fired her specifically because of the video.

If she can prove that that's why she was fired, they may be willing to settle for what would have been a few years pay for her, 75k roughly.

2chainz lawyers aren't working pro bono. He has a team of them, and he's getting charged upwards of 200 (more likely upwards of 400) dollars an hour for each of them. If the case is allowed to progress into discovery, each of those lawyers charging that much per hour really adds up, and he'll be paying way more than 75k in his own legal fees before it's all said and done.

This is why frivolous law suits work. It'll cost much more to fight than settle, and the plaintiff has nothing to lose.

Please please take this to trial would make for one of the best court records of all time.

Hey everyone, I am making the transition to Voat the best I can after browsing Reddit for nearly four years. After all that has happened in the past week I thought that if I am going to be part of a new community it would be the right thing and try to contribute. I have an idea that would maybe help the majority of Reddit users switch to Voat. Many Reddit users stay at Reddit because they have built a reputation and have many achievements on their accounts like large amounts of karma and "trophies" that they achieved throughout their Reddit career. Maybe we can figure a way where when a Reddit user makes their Voat account they put in a unique code that would make their Voat account as valuable as their Reddit account. I feel this would in a way incentivize new Voat users who spent years building their accounts at Reddit to come to Voat. I am sure there are flaws with this idea but I think it's a great way to break down that barrier some users face when they essentially "start over". I am also aware Voat has other priorities (like being able to handle the spike in traffic when something happens at Reddit). I think this would be a good way to obtain more Voat users who contributed on Reddit to contribute quality content at Voat. I am absolutely open to any suggestions, criticisms, or whatever is thrown my way. Just trying to contribute.

Nigel Farage: The European Project Plan Has Failed. Farage tells Greece to take back their democracy.
That was a really powerful speech, i wish more politicians would stand up for the people and not the money.

Joining an organization like the EU will inevitably put reigns on your own sovereignty. Such constraints on national sovereignty can and do create situations where the government is forced to go against the will of its people.

In this manner, the EU and other organizations can be undemocratic and Nigel is correct.

However, I believe that Greece shows the integral failings of democracy instead of failing at democracy because of the EU.

Simply put, a majority of people can be easily convinced to support measures that increase their standard of living in the short term. But nothing anywhere says that these measures are beneficial to the long term well-being of the nation and its people. You can be a corrupt asswipe politician leaching away your nation's future into your own pockets and still be a 100% democratically elected leader as long as you have majority popular support (which Nigel Farage does not have, BTW).

Had Greece not joined the EU, this problem would still have remained. The only real difference would have been the lack of easy money for corrupt asswipes to use for popular support funding. I'm not convinced that this would have made a huge difference, unless there is evidence that these corrupt asswipes were forced onto Greece through constraints on sovereignty.
